INSERT INTO nexmark_q4
SELECT
    Q.category,
    AVG(Q.final)
FROM (
    SELECT MAX(B.price) AS final, A.category
    FROM auction A, bid B
    WHERE A.id = B.auction AND B.`dateTime` BETWEEN A.`dateTime` AND A.expires
    GROUP BY A.id, A.category
) Q
GROUP BY Q.category;

Splitting into two chained views (inner view GROUP BY A.id, A.category with MAX; outer GROUP BY category with SUM and COUNT) still needs F8 in the form of view-over-view, which v0 does not demonstrate.

items.query:
INSERT INTO nexmark_q5
SELECT AuctionBids.auction, AuctionBids.num
 FROM (
   SELECT
     auction,
     count(*) AS num,
     window_start AS starttime,
     window_end AS endtime
     FROM TABLE(
             HOP(TABLE bid, DESCRIPTOR(`dateTime`), INTERVAL '2' SECOND, INTERVAL '10' SECOND))
     GROUP BY auction, window_start, window_end
 ) AS AuctionBids
 JOIN (
   SELECT
     max(CountBids.num) AS maxn,
     CountBids.starttime,
     CountBids.endtime
   FROM (
     SELECT
       count(*) AS num,
       window_start AS starttime,
       window_end AS endtime
     FROM TABLE(
                HOP(TABLE bid, DESCRIPTOR(`dateTime`), INTERVAL '2' SECOND, INTERVAL '10' SECOND))
     GROUP BY auction, window_start, window_end
     ) AS CountBids
   GROUP BY CountBids.starttime, CountBids.endtime
 ) AS MaxBids
 ON AuctionBids.starttime = MaxBids.starttime AND
    AuctionBids.endtime = MaxBids.endtime AND
    AuctionBids.num >= MaxBids.maxn;

items.adapted_rewrite: Replace HOP with an app-maintained window-membership table bid_win(auction, win_start, win_end) holding 5 rows per bid (10s window, 2s slide); bag rewrite at the root. The two window/group derived tables, the MAX, the (start,end) two-column join key and the num >= maxn non-equi condition remain.

items.notes: Core logic (per-window hottest auctions) is meaningful in SQLite given a membership table, but the answer then holds every window ever seen, not the window-close emissions of Flink. Fan-out of 5 changes the maintenance workload.

items.query:
INSERT INTO nexmark_q6
SELECT
    Q.seller,
    AVG(Q.price) OVER
        (PARTITION BY Q.seller ORDER BY Q.`dateTime` ROWS BETWEEN 10 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
FROM (
    SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY A.id, A.seller ORDER BY B.price DESC) AS rownum
    FROM (SELECT A.id, A.seller, B.price, B.`dateTime`
        FROM auction AS A,
            bid AS B
        WHERE A.id = B.auction
            and B.`dateTime` between A.`dateTime` and A.expires)
    WHERE rownum <= 1
) AS Q;

f15_detail.detail: ordered rolling frame AVG(...) OVER (PARTITION BY seller ORDER BY dateTime ROWS BETWEEN 10 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) over a retracting input; the file itself carries a TODO saying Flink SQL does not support it

items.adapted_rewrite: None. Even a corrected form needs winning-bid top-1 per auction (ROW_NUMBER, F9), then a per-seller rolling average over the last 10 closed auctions ordered by time, which is an ordered window frame.

items.notes: Could be reclassified fits_with (all F9) if ivmlite ever implements generic window functions with retraction; ordered-frame maintenance is the blocking part.

INSERT INTO nexmark_q7
SELECT B.auction, B.price, B.bidder, B.`dateTime`, B.extra
from bid B
JOIN (
  SELECT MAX(price) AS maxprice, window_end as `dateTime`
  FROM TABLE(
          TUMBLE(TABLE bid, DESCRIPTOR(`dateTime`), INTERVAL '10' SECOND))
  GROUP BY window_start, window_end
) B1
ON B.price = B1.maxprice
WHERE B.`dateTime` BETWEEN B1.`dateTime`  - INTERVAL '10' SECOND AND B1.`dateTime`;

items.adapted_rewrite: Add an app-maintained INTEGER column win_end = (dateTime/10000+1)*10000 to bid (TUMBLE is [start,end), so floor division is exact); derived table B1 becomes SELECT MAX(price), win_end FROM bid GROUP BY win_end; keep the join `B.price = B1.maxprice AND B.dateTime BETWEEN B1.win_end-10000 AND B1.win_end` including its closed upper bound, so a bid exactly on a window boundary behaves as in the original; bag rewrite at the root.

items.notes: 'Highest bid per 10s bucket' is meaningful in SQLite with a stored bucket. Flink emits per closed window; the SQLite view holds all buckets.

items.query:
INSERT INTO nexmark_q8
SELECT P.id, P.name, P.starttime
FROM (
  SELECT id, name,
        window_start AS starttime,
        window_end AS endtime
  FROM TABLE(
            TUMBLE(TABLE person, DESCRIPTOR(`dateTime`), INTERVAL '10' SECOND))
  GROUP BY id, name, window_start, window_end
) P
JOIN (
  SELECT seller,
        window_start AS starttime,
        window_end AS endtime
  FROM TABLE(
        TUMBLE(TABLE auction, DESCRIPTOR(`dateTime`), INTERVAL '10' SECOND))
  GROUP BY seller, window_start, window_end
) A
ON P.id = A.seller AND P.starttime = A.starttime AND P.endtime = A.endtime;

f15_detail.name: dedup
f15_detail.detail: GROUP BY with no aggregate on both derived tables (set/DISTINCT semantics)

items.adapted_rewrite: Add win_start INTEGER = (dateTime/10000)*10000 to person and auction, plus a composite TEXT join key on each side (person.pk = id||':'||win_start, auction.sk = seller||':'||win_start) so the join is a single same-typed pair. Collapse both derived tables into the join and use the bag rewrite GROUP BY P.id, P.name, P.win_start + COUNT(*). Presence of a group equals presence of the original row; multiplicity becomes the number of auctions by that seller in the window instead of 1.
items.adapted_confidence_reason: Set semantics are lost; it is faithful only after collapsing multiplicity to presence, and it assumes person (id,name,window) is already unique.
items.confidence_reason: Two TUMBLE windows are F12; the join also needs a two-column key.
items.notes: 'People who both joined and opened an auction in the same 10s bucket' is meaningful in SQLite with stored buckets.

INSERT INTO nexmark_q9
SELECT
    id, itemName, description, initialBid, reserve, `dateTime`, expires, seller, category, extra,
    auction, bidder, price, bid_dateTime, bid_extra
FROM (
   SELECT A.*, B.auction, B.bidder, B.price, B.`dateTime` AS bid_dateTime, B.extra AS bid_extra,
     ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY A.id ORDER BY B.price DESC, B.`dateTime` ASC) AS rownum
   FROM auction A, bid B
   WHERE A.id = B.auction AND B.`dateTime` BETWEEN A.`dateTime` AND A.expires
)
WHERE rownum <= 1;

f15_detail.name: ordered
f15_detail.detail: gap-based session merging: an insert inside a gap can merge two sessions and a delete can split one, so the grouping itself is order/gap dependent

items.adapted_rewrite: None. Sessionisation in plain SQL needs LAG/window functions and a cumulative sum over each bidder's ordered bids; one new bid can renumber every later session.

CREATE VIEW B AS SELECT *, PROCTIME() as p_time FROM bid;
INSERT INTO nexmark_q12
SELECT
    bidder,
    count(*) as bid_count,
    window_start AS starttime,
    window_end AS endtime
FROM TABLE(
        TUMBLE(TABLE B, DESCRIPTOR(p_time), INTERVAL '10' SECOND))
GROUP BY bidder, window_start, window_end;

flink_specific_constructs: PROCTIME() processing-time attribute (wall clock at arrival)
TUMBLE(TABLE B, DESCRIPTOR(p_time), 10s) over a view
items.adapted_rewrite: Stamp each bid at insert time with INTEGER p_start (arrival time floored to 10s) and p_end = p_start+10000 (column DEFAULT or insert trigger), then GROUP BY bidder, p_start, p_end + COUNT(*).
items.adapted_confidence_reason: Result depends on when rows were inserted, not on row contents, so it is reproducible only because the stamp is stored; it is a different (arrival-time) semantics and meaningless as a replayable benchmark.
items.confidence_reason: Processing-time windows depend on the wall clock at arrival, which is F12 by the taxonomy.
items.notes: Bucket counts per bidder per arrival bucket is runnable on v0 once the stamp column exists.

INSERT INTO nexmark_q13
SELECT
    B.auction,
    B.bidder,
    B.price,
    B.`dateTime`,
    S.`value`
FROM (SELECT *, PROCTIME() as p_time FROM bid) B
JOIN side_input FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF B.p_time AS S
ON mod(B.auction, 10000) = S.key;

schema.note: Preflight STRICT mapping (docs/bench/m2b-preflight): BIGINT->INTEGER, VARCHAR->TEXT, TIMESTAMP(3)->INTEGER (epoch unit unspecified by preflight). flink_specific_constructs: temporal join: side_input FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF B.p_time
join key is an expression mod(B.auction,10000)
items.adapted_rewrite: Bag rewrite on (auction, bidder, price, dateTime, value) + COUNT(*); an app-maintained INTEGER column auction_mod10000 on bid; ordinary inner join ON bid.auction_mod10000 = side_input.key. The temporal (as-of-arrival) lookup is replaced by a snapshot join, which is exact only if side_input never changes after the bids it joins.
items.adapted_confidence_reason: Equivalent only for a frozen side table; any later change to side_input would retroactively rewrite old joined rows, which the temporal join would not.
items.confidence_reason: A FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF temporal join is explicitly F12.
items.notes: Nexmark loads side_input once from a file, so the frozen assumption holds in the benchmark. The expression join key is the additional gap.

-- CREATE FUNCTION count_char AS 'com.github.nexmark.flink.udf.CountChar';
INSERT INTO nexmark_q14
SELECT 
    auction,
    bidder,
    0.908 * price as price,
    CASE
        WHEN HOUR(`dateTime`) >= 8 AND HOUR(`dateTime`) <= 18 THEN 'dayTime'
        WHEN HOUR(`dateTime`) <= 6 OR HOUR(`dateTime`) >= 20 THEN 'nightTime'
        ELSE 'otherTime'
    END AS bidTimeType,
    `dateTime`,
    extra,
    count_char(extra, 'c') AS c_counts
FROM bid
WHERE 0.908 * price > 1000000 AND 0.908 * price < 50000000;

f15_detail.name: flink-fn
f15_detail.detail: count_char UDF (Java, counts bytes equal to the first byte of the argument); replaceable by length(CAST(x AS BLOB)) - length(CAST(replace(x,'c','') AS BLOB)) with NULL mapped to 0, so not blocking

items.adapted_rewrite: Bag rewrite + app-maintained columns: price_eur_milli = price*908 (INTEGER), bid_time_type (CASE over the hour), c_counts (byte count of 'c' in extra, 0 for NULL), and a 0/1 flag in_range = (price*908 > 1000000000 AND price*908 < 50000000000) replacing the two expression predicates with `WHERE in_range = 1`.
items.adapted_confidence_reason: Every computed output and the filter live in stored columns, so the view merely stores what the application computes; the integer scaling is exact.
items.confidence_reason: Expressions, CASE, a UDF and an AND of two expression predicates over a single table.
items.notes: The comparison bounds scale by 1000 along with the stored milli price.

INSERT INTO nexmark_q15
SELECT
     DATE_FORMAT(`dateTime`, 'yyyy-MM-dd') as `day`,
     count(*) AS total_bids,
     count(*) filter (where price < 10000) AS rank1_bids,
     count(*) filter (where price >= 10000 and price < 1000000) AS rank2_bids,
     count(*) filter (where price >= 1000000) AS rank3_bids,
     count(distinct bidder) AS total_bidders,
     count(distinct bidder) filter (where price < 10000) AS rank1_bidders,
     count(distinct bidder) filter (where price >= 10000 and price < 1000000) AS rank2_bidders,
     count(distinct bidder) filter (where price >= 1000000) AS rank3_bidders,
     count(distinct auction) AS total_auctions,
     count(distinct auction) filter (where price < 10000) AS rank1_auctions,
     count(distinct auction) filter (where price >= 10000 and price < 1000000) AS rank2_auctions,
     count(distinct auction) filter (where price >= 1000000) AS rank3_auctions
FROM bid
GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(`dateTime`, 'yyyy-MM-dd');

INSERT INTO nexmark_q16
SELECT
    channel,
    DATE_FORMAT(`dateTime`, 'yyyy-MM-dd') as `day`,
    max(DATE_FORMAT(`dateTime`, 'HH:mm')) as `minute`,

INSERT INTO nexmark_q21
SELECT
    auction, bidder, price, channel,
    CASE
        WHEN lower(channel) = 'apple' THEN '0'
        WHEN lower(channel) = 'google' THEN '1'
        WHEN lower(channel) = 'facebook' THEN '2'
        WHEN lower(channel) = 'baidu' THEN '3'
        ELSE REGEXP_EXTRACT(url, '(&|^)channel_id=([^&]*)', 2)
        END
    AS channel_id FROM bid
    where REGEXP_EXTRACT(url, '(&|^)channel_id=([^&]*)', 2) is not null or
          lower(channel) in ('apple', 'google', 'facebook', 'baidu');
